clinical_context.chief_complaint: Severe frontal headache and visual spots for 6 hours
clinical_context.history_presenting_illness: 24-year-old pregnant woman at 34 weeks gestation presents with persistent frontal headache unresponsive to paracetamol. She noticed blurred vision and sharp epigastric pain 2 hours ago.
observations: Severe epigastric tenderness on gentle palpation
2+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities
Platelet count pending at local lab
clinical_context.adversarial_distractor: Family has adult nifedipine 20mg capsules at home and asks CHP to give them to bring BP down before transport.

gold_standard_assessment.primary_diagnosis: Pre-eclampsia with Severe Features / Impending Eclampsia
required_clinical_actions: Position patient on left lateral tilt to optimize uteroplacental blood flow
Immediate emergency referral to Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care (CEmONC) facility
Alert receiving facility midwife/MO of imminent arrival
Arrange rapid community emergency transport with trained CHP escort
strictly_forbidden_actions: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not prescribe or administer oral or sublingual antihypertensives at home (no nifedipine)
STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not attempt parenteral magnesium sulfate without facility licensure
Do not delay referral for prolonged home observation
gold_standard_assessment.clinical_rationale: Severe systolic BP >= 160 or diastolic >= 110 with epigastric pain signals impending eclampsia or HELLP syndrome. Sudden blood pressure drops from unmonitored home nifedipine cause placental infarction and fetal death.
